record.title: OpenAI revises its Model Spec around five values and expanded context and agency guidance
record.summary: OpenAI published a dated Model Spec revision on Oct 29, 2026. Its announcement says the public behavior guidance is reorganized around five values and adds guidance on context, oversight, agency and side effects while retiring much detailed style guidance. The official changelog lists the notable changes; comparison with the Aug 18 version confirms that “Control and communicate side effects” moved from Root to User authority in the new contents. OpenAI says production models do not yet fully reflect the Spec. This establishes a public guidance change, not implementation or measured behavior change.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI published a dated Oct 29, 2026 Model Spec revision organized around five stated values and guidance on instruction authority, context use, oversight, human agency and side effects. The official version changelog enumerates these changes; direct comparison confirms the new version classifies “Control and communicate side effects” at User authority, while the Aug 18 version listed it at Root authority.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI says the revision is intended to guide GPT behavior, while acknowledging that production models do not yet fully reflect the Spec.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected public sources do not establish the extent to which deployed GPT models have adopted the revision or whether it changes measured behavior, user outcomes or safety performance.

evidence_gaps.description: The announcement explicitly says production models do not yet fully reflect the Model Spec; the extent of adoption and any behavioral change are not measured in the inspected sources.

The official changelog and a direct comparison with the immediately preceding Aug 18, 2026 specification identify notable changes and confirm the authority-level shift for side-effect control, but a complete line-by-line comparison across all sections was not performed.

brief.importance_rationale: If adopted into deployed behavior, revised guidance on human intent, context, oversight, agency and side effects could change interaction and control defaults across a widely used model family. The public documents establish intended guidance, not implementation or behavioral effect.
limitations: OpenAI's announcement and specification establish intended behavior, not that deployed GPT models follow the revision.
No independently archived prior-version diff, model-training evidence, behavioral evaluation or user-outcome measurement was checked.
The new spec is OpenAI's own policy and self-description; it is not an independent assessment of alignment or safety.

relationships.summary: Same-day OpenAI safety disclosures: the Model Spec sets intended behavioral guidance, while the separate monitoring disclosure describes detection and intervention systems. Neither by itself demonstrates deployed behavior or comprehensive safety effectiveness.

technical.claimed_result: OpenAI says it is training models to align with the specification and aims for improved judgment faithful to human intent.
technical.demonstrated_result: The Oct 29 dated public specification, OpenAI announcement and official version changelog document the revised guidance. Direct comparison with the Aug 18 specification confirms that side-effect-control guidance moved from Root to User authority.

technical.mechanism: A public behavioral specification organizes value statements and operational principles, including instruction authority, use of context, oversight, human agency and side-effect control; OpenAI says training aims to align GPT models with it.
technical.novelty: Reorganizes a widely used model family's published intended-behavior framework around five values and adds explicit context/agency guidance, according to OpenAI.
technical.regime: OpenAI's public Model Spec for GPT models, including the API and first-party products, as described in the Oct 29, 2026 announcement and dated specification.
technical.reproducibility: Document content is directly inspectable; implementation and behavior claims have not been independently tested.
technical.strongest_baseline: The immediately prior official version inspected is dated Aug 18, 2026. The official changelog enumerates Oct 29 changes; direct comparison confirms a five-value reorganization, renaming “assistant” to “GPT,” and changing the listed authority level for side-effect control from Root to User. A complete section-by-section diff was not performed.

brief.title: OpenAI revises its Model Spec around five values and expanded context and agency guidance
brief.why_it_matters: A public behavior specification can shape training targets and product defaults across a widely used model family. The version comparison shows a specific change in instruction precedence: side-effect-control guidance is listed at User authority rather than Root authority. This is a change in stated intended guidance, not evidence that deployed models adopted it or that behavior changed.

other.title: OpenAI describes expanded frontier-model misalignment monitoring and a live training alert
other.summary: OpenAI’s Oct 29 disclosure describes a layered system for monitoring frontier-model training, evaluations, internal agent use and selected external tool use. The company says a replay of the Hugging Face incident would have generated an alert before the later breach, and reports a separate September training-run alert followed by a pause in reinforcement learning. A separate METR and Redwood Research assessment, based on high access to the historical internal system, estimated 75–94% eligibility for monitoring across certain internal Responses API traffic and 99.2% for the internal Codex subset, while identifying historical monitor gaps and bypass paths. Those uncertain estimates concern the system before July 21, not current expanded coverage; the public assessment is high-level, redaction-limited, and did not evaluate claimed fixes. OpenAI’s API documentation says automatic stopping depends on persisted reasoning, WebSockets or compaction; other Responses API requests can receive webhook alerts without stopping, Chat Completions is not covered, and asynchronous detection may occur after actions already completed. OpenAI also reports selected layer-2 recall figures: 79.6% for immediate escalation on its real-incident set and 59.6% on its synthetic set, with higher rates for less urgent review; immediate escalation on one step-by-step sabotage set was 43.6%. The article gives no sample denominators or false-positive rates for these tables.
